data.title: Directory Enumeration Unrestricted for Standard Users
data.summary:
Any authenticated account could enumerate users, groups, computers, trusts and
access-control relationships across the directory, and the queries supporting that
enumeration were not logged or alerted on.
data.description:
Directory read access is required for the environment to function, so the enumeration
itself cannot simply be removed. What it provides to an operator, however, is the complete
map: every privileged group, every delegation, every trust, and every path from a
compromised account to a valuable one.

That map is what converts a single compromised workstation into a planned route to domain
compromise, and it is obtainable within minutes of the first authentication.

Since prevention is largely unavailable, the controls that matter are reducing what the map
reveals — fewer excessive rights and shorter paths — and detecting the enumeration itself,
which has a distinctive high-volume query signature.
data.recommendation:
* Run the same path analysis the attacker would, and remove the shortest routes from
  ordinary accounts to privileged ones.
* Enable directory auditing and alert on high-volume or unusual query patterns from
  non-administrative accounts.
* Remove unnecessary delegation and nested privileged group membership, which is what the
  enumeration finds.
* Consider decoy accounts whose only purpose is to be found by enumeration and alerted on.
data.short_recommendation: Run attacker path analysis yourself and shorten the paths it finds.
